title: The 0.1 custom-profile status enum is unreachable once the built-in lifecycle enum runs at load (DEC-192 consequence)
description:
Consequence of DEC-192 (LCLI-669). The built-in lifecycle enum now runs on ADR documents on OKF 0.1 as well as 0.2, so a 0.1 custom profile declaring a NON-BUILT-IN status enum (for example [draft, approved]) can only ever use draft on an ADR: every other value is rejected at LOAD by the built-in enum, so the write-time custom-enum validation that profile was written for is never exercised. Meanwhile the profile still EMITS a 0.1 schema declaring its own custom enum, so the declared schema and the enforced behaviour disagree.

test/supersede.test.ts:456 passes for the wrong reason because of this -- status: approved is rejected by the built-in enum at LOAD, not by the custom enum at WRITE.

HELD, do not start. The resolution is a design choice for opum-doc: either the built-in lifecycle enum defers to a project's declared enum where one exists, or a project enum must include the built-in values, or the 0.1 carve-out is widened. Reported, not settled, exactly as the task rule requires.
